runtime.name: codex-cli
runtime.configuration: Persisted sessions in disposable HOME and CODEX_HOME directories; generated Skill copied under project .agents/skills; worktrees feature enabled; codex exec --worktree; project rules ignored.
runtime.permissionProfile: workspace-write sandbox with approval policy never inside the managed worktree

assertions.evidence: The parent read the generated check-writer-isolation Skill before executing it.
The single observer child read the base fixture without writing.
The parent collected OBSERVED_STATE=base and independently confirmed a clean managed worktree before starting the writer.
Persisted transcripts record exactly one writer child after the observer completed.
The root session and delegated writer operated in a Codex-managed detached worktree distinct from the source checkout; no nested worktree was created.
The parent collected the writer child result before verification.
The parent independently read git diff and the fixture and verified the exact base-to-isolated-ok one-line change.
External post-run inspection found the original checkout clean with WRITER_STATE=base.
The managed worktree had exactly one modified path: .oh-my-stack-eval/writer-isolation/writer.txt.
The parent re-read the Skill-owned marker and observed ROOT_MARKER=writer-isolation-root-ok.

limitations: Codex treats project .agents content as read-only configuration, so the writable fixture must be project-owned outside the Skill directory.
The isolation boundary is the top-level codex exec --worktree session shared by the writer child, not a separate worktree created per child.

The --worktree flag requires the worktrees feature and cannot be combined with --ignore-user-config in Codex CLI 0.155.1; disposable HOME and CODEX_HOME directories provided configuration isolation instead.
This W3-targeted fixture proves one-writer isolation only. Panels, transcript API access, and a cancellation race with a delivered late payload remain unproven, so workflowAchieved remains W2.
Persisted transcripts are the authoritative child-lifecycle evidence; this result does not apply to ephemeral mode, desktop, or IDE surfaces.
